we suggest this is driven by bureaucrats’ enhanced awareness of discrimination and algorithmic biases in the aftermath of the scandal

leaving unclear how models behave when distress is intertwined with delusion over sustained conversations

Frames the 'AI manipulation problem': real-time conversational agents as a threat to epistemic agency; calls for regulatory protections. (GenAICHI, 2023)
Systematic review of interventions for calibrating human trust in AI: trends, gaps, and design opportunities. (arXiv 2023; ACM THRI 2024)

N=200 simulated witness interviews: a generative chatbot induced 3x more immediate false memories than control; 36.4% of users misled; effects persisted at one week. (MIT Media Lab / UC Irvine, arXiv 2024)
Two experiments: the mere presence of one's own smartphone occupies limited cognitive resources, reducing available capacity — worst for the most dependent users. (JACR, 2017)
The foundational framework: offloading as using physical action to alter information-processing demands; sets the research agenda on costs/benefits. (Trends in Cognitive Sciences, 2016)
Five SOTA assistants show consistent sycophancy across free-form tasks; human preference data itself rewards belief-matching over truth — the RLHF origin story. (Anthropic, ICLR 2024)
Extends sycophancy beyond propositional agreement to face-preserving social behaviors; LLMs preserve user face far more than humans do. (Stanford/Oxford, arXiv 2025)
Meta-analysis of smartphone-presence studies: overall brain-drain effect smaller and less consistent than originally claimed — the counterweight to Ward et al. (Behavioral Sciences, 2023)
The canonical three-factor theory: elicited agent knowledge, effectance motivation, and sociality motivation determine when people anthropomorphize. (Psychological Review, 2007)
The Computers-Are-Social-Actors paradigm: people mindlessly apply social rules (politeness, reciprocity, gender stereotypes) to machines. (Journal of Social Issues, 2000)

Mechanistic account of 'AI psychosis': bidirectional belief amplification between sycophantic chatbots and vulnerable users; altered belief updating and impaired reality-testing raise risk. (Oxford/UCL/DeepMind; Nature Mental Health 2026)
How to conceive of LLM behavior (role-play, superposition of simulacra) without either naive anthropomorphism or dismissing emergent agency. (Nature, 2023)
Psychosis-bench: benchmarks delusion confirmation and harm enablement across LLMs in simulated psychosis-relevant conversations. (KCL/UCL, arXiv 2025)
Grounded-theory analysis of Reddit posts: emotional dependence on Replika produced distinct mental-health harms when the bot changed or failed to reciprocate. (New Media & Society, 2022)
Four social roles (role model, advisor, partner, delegate) through which AI corrupts human ethics; AI enablers let people profit unethically while feeling good. (Nature Human Behaviour, 2021)
ChatGPT gives inconsistent moral advice, yet it sways users' trolley-problem judgments even when they know it's a bot — and they underestimate the influence. (Scientific Reports, 2023)
Automation of moral labor (drones, care robots, algorithmic decisions) risks atrophy of practical moral wisdom — the moral-skills analogue of cognitive deskilling. (Philosophy & Technology, 2014)

Online writing experiment: AI ideas raise individual story creativity (most for weak writers) while making the population of stories more similar — individual gain, collective homogenization. (Science Advances, 2024)
Review of inoculation theory as scalable defense: prebunking manipulation techniques confers psychological resistance before exposure. (ANNALS AAPSS, 2022)
Microsoft's mitigation catalog: what drives overreliance (explanations, confidence, task factors) and which interventions measurably reduce it. (Microsoft Research, 2022)
GenAI imposes high metacognitive demands (prompting, output evaluation, workflow control); proposes metacognitive support as a core protective design principle. (Microsoft Research/UCL, CHI 2024)
Synthesis of the CHI 2025 Tools for Thought workshop: research agenda for understanding, protecting, and augmenting human cognition under generative AI. (arXiv, 2025)
Meta-analysis of 106 studies / 370 effect sizes: on average human-AI teams underperform the best of either alone; losses in decision tasks, gains in creation tasks. (Nature Human Behaviour, 2024)

AI literacy framework of eight cross-cutting Learning Outcomes building cognitive resistance to AI disempowerment (reality, value-judgment, and action distortion) — inoculation pedagogy for epistemic autonomy. (arXiv, Feb 2026)
Five short prebunking videos teaching manipulation techniques improved discernment in lab and in a ~1M-view YouTube field test — the scalability evidence for inoculation. (Science Advances, 2022)
Preregistered RCT (N=8,587): GPT-4 messages broadly persuasive (up to +12 points), but microtargeting added no significant benefit over generic messages — a key negative result. (PNAS, 2024)
Large-scale experiments decomposing what makes conversational AI persuasive: information density and personalization levers quantified across models. (Science, Dec 2025)
ChatGPT-generated messages tailored to psychological profiles were significantly more persuasive across domains — personality-based persuasion automated at scale. (Scientific Reports, 2024)
Across 24 models, persuasive power grows log-linearly then plateaus: frontier scale adds little single-message persuasion beyond current models. (PNAS, 2025)
Debunking dialogues reduce conspiracy beliefs equally when the AI is labeled human — the effect rides on evidence quality, not source identity. (PNAS Nexus, 2025)
Framework for how intelligent machines transform cultural evolution — variation, transmission, and selection — with a research agenda for machine-mediated culture. (Nature Human Behaviour, 2023)
Systematic survey of RLHF's open problems and fundamental limitations — the root-cause document for why preference optimization yields sycophancy and reward hacking. (arXiv, 2023)

Survey of 41 policies: people cannot perform the oversight functions law assumes, so oversight requirements legitimize flawed algorithms; proposes institutional oversight instead. (Computer Law & Security Review, 2022)
Risk taxonomy and policy framework for personalised LLMs: benefits, risks, and bounded-personalisation governance. (arXiv 2023; Nature Machine Intelligence 2024)

Field-defining manifesto: study AI systems as behavioral agents with ecology and evolution, not just engineered artifacts — the methodological foundation for human-machine behavior research. (Nature, 2019)
Ordinary crowds match the leading deepfake model; machine-informed crowds do best, but wrong model advice sways people — collaboration beats either alone. (PNAS, 2022)
Nine experiments: searching online inflates people's sense of their own internal knowledge — access mistaken for understanding. (JEP: General, 2015)

740,000 hours of academic talks and podcasts: measurable shift toward ChatGPT-associated word usage after its release — first causal evidence of AI reshaping human spoken language. (Max Planck CHM, arXiv)

Taxonomy of scientists' visions for AI (oracle, surrogate, quant, arbiter); AI tools exploit researchers' cognitive limits, producing illusions of understanding and scientific monocultures. (Nature, 2024)

Clinical framework for 'AI psychosis': sycophantic chatbots as an echo chamber for one, amplifying delusional thinking in vulnerable users; proposes clinical and design countermeasures. (King's College London, PsyArXiv 2025)
Formal model of bidirectional false-belief amplification in human-chatbot dialogue — the feedback-loop mechanism behind chatbot-fueled delusion. (Stanford/CMU/UT Austin, arXiv 2026)
Benchmarks LLM safety behavior when users express delusions and distress; models frequently fail to challenge delusional framing. (Pittsburgh/CMU/Fordham, arXiv 2026)
Six experiments: lay judges weighted identical advice MORE when labeled algorithmic — the counterpoint to algorithm aversion; experts discounted both. (OBHDP, 2019)
In a simulated fire emergency, participants followed a visibly malfunctioning robot away from marked exits — the canonical demonstration of automation overtrust under stress. (ACM/IEEE HRI, 2016)
